title: Understanding Prediction, Classification, and Generation in AI
introduction: This lesson explains three basic ways AI produces results: predicting numbers, classifying items, and generating new content. Knowing these helps you see how AI works in everyday tools.

sections.heading: Prediction: Estimating Future Values
sections.subheading: How AI guesses numbers or amounts
paragraphs: Prediction means the AI looks at past data and guesses a future number or outcome. It does not create new categories, it simply forecasts a value.
For example, a weather service uses temperature history to predict tomorrow's high temperature.

example.title: Weather Forecast Example
example.content: A weather app predicts tomorrow's temperature as 25°C based on past data.

sections.heading: Classification: Sorting into Groups
sections.subheading: How AI decides which category something belongs to
paragraphs: Classification is when AI looks at an item and decides which of several groups it fits into. The groups are defined beforehand.
The AI learns patterns that tell it how to place new items into the right group.

example.title: Email Spam Filter
example.content: An email system classifies incoming messages as "spam" or "not spam" using learned patterns.

sections.heading: Generation: Creating New Content
sections.subheading: How AI produces original text, images, or music
paragraphs: Generation means the AI creates something new that did not exist before, such as sentences, pictures, or melodies.
It uses learned knowledge to produce fresh output that matches a style or instruction.

example.title: Story Writing Bot
example.content: A language model writes a short story about a brave rabbit, creating sentences that did not exist before.

sections.heading: Seeing These Tasks in Everyday AI
sections.subheading: Real‑world tools that use prediction, classification, or generation
paragraphs: Many apps combine these tasks. A navigation app predicts travel time, a photo app classifies images, and a chat bot generates replies.
Understanding which task is used helps you trust and use AI better.

example.title: Smartphone Voice Assistant
example.content: When you ask your phone for a joke, it generates new text; when it suggests a route, it predicts travel time; when it shows photos of cats, it classifies images.

practice.title: Identify AI Task Types
practice.instruction: Find three examples of AI you use daily (e.g., weather app, photo app, chat bot). Write next to each whether it is a prediction, classification, or generation.

keyTakeaways: Prediction lets AI estimate numbers or future events based on past data.
Classification lets AI assign items to predefined categories.
Generation lets AI create new text, images, or other content that did not exist before.

mcqs.question: What is the main difference between prediction and classification in AI?
options: Prediction outputs a numeric value, while classification assigns an item to a predefined category.
Prediction creates new content, while classification forecasts future events.
Prediction sorts items into groups, while classification estimates numbers.
Prediction and classification are the same task performed differently.
mcqs.explanation: Prediction gives a numeric forecast; classification puts an item into an existing group.

mcqs.question: Which AI task does a photo app perform when it shows you pictures of cats?
mcqs.explanation: The app looks at images and decides which ones belong to the "cat" category, which is classification.

mcqs.question: Which statement best describes AI generation?
options: It predicts future numbers based on past data.
It sorts items into predefined groups.
It creates new text, images, or music that did not exist before.
It assigns labels to items using learned patterns.
mcqs.explanation: Generation produces original content such as sentences or pictures, unlike prediction or classification.

mcqs.question: A navigation app suggests a route and estimates travel time. Which AI task is used for estimating travel time?
mcqs.explanation: Estimating travel time is a forecast of a future numeric value, which is a prediction task.

mcqs.question: In the email spam filter example, what does the AI learn to do?
mcqs.explanation: The spam filter learns patterns that let it place each incoming message into the predefined categories of spam or not spam.
